extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and researchers learning algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, theorems, and exercises about differentials (cotangent sheaf), conormal/normal sheaves, and smoothness of schemes/varieties; includes concrete computations (P^n, P^1, curves) and base-change/localization behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Normal/conormal sheaf for effective Cartier divisors
rubrics_metrics.description: If D is an effective Cartier divisor in X, then the conormal sheaf N^∨_{D/X} is O(-D)|_D (an invertible sheaf), and the normal sheaf is O(D)|_D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This justifies the earlier definition of normal bundles for effective Cartier divisors. Note: this may seem surprising when D is singular (e.g., union of axes in A^2) because geometric intuition about tubular neighborhoods need not hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 21.2.16 — regular sequence gives I/I^2 free
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is Noetherian and I is generated by a regular sequence x1,...,xr, then the map γ:(A/I)^⊕r → I/I^2 sending (a1,...,ar) ↦ Σ ai xi exhibits I/I^2 as a free A/I-module of rank r with basis the xi. Consequently, for a codimension-r regular embedding, the (co)normal sheaf is locally free of rank r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses localization (injectivity/stalk-local condition) and the nonzerodivisor property of the regular sequence. See referenced exercises/theorems for details; part (b) follows from (a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher graded pieces: I^n/I^{n+1} = Sym^n(I/I^2)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a regular embedding with ideal sheaf I, each graded piece I^n/I^{n+1} is locally free and equals Sym^n(I/I^2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as a related (harder) fact and referenced to Theorem 22.3.8 for proof and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of B-linear derivation and universal property of Ω_{A/B}
rubrics_metrics.description: A B-linear derivation d:A → M (M an A-module) is a B-linear map satisfying Leibniz: d(fg)=f dg + g df. The module Ω_{A/B} with the universal derivation d:A→Ω_{A/B} has the universal property that any B-linear derivation d':A→M factors uniquely through Ω_{A/B}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: d/dx on k[x]; evaluation of derivative at 0 as a derivation to k. The universal property implies uniqueness up to unique isomorphism; constructive and universal definitions are complementary and useful in exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of differentials (affine case) / base-change behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a commutative square of rings A'→A over B'→B there is a natural A'-module homomorphism A'⊗_A Ω_{A/B} → Ω_{A'/B'}. If the square is a tensor (co-Cartesian) diagram (A' ≅ B'⊗_B A), then this map is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Exercise 21.2.K; the special case B=B' is important. Some proofs are trickier than they first appear. Use this to deduce base-change compatibilities of Ω in affines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: For a ring map φ:B→A and multiplicative subsets S⊂A, T⊂B with φ(T)⊂S, the natural map S^{-1}Ω_{A/B} → Ω_{S^{-1}A / T^{-1}B} is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is Exercise 21.2.L and follows the intuition of 'vertical cotangent vectors' surviving localization; an important special case is T={1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentials for field extensions / separably generated case
rubrics_metrics.description: If K/k is separably generated by t1,...,tn (i.e., t_i form a transcendence basis and K/k(t1,...,tn) is algebraic separable), then Ω_{K/k} is a free K-module with basis dt1,...,dtn. Compute Ω_{k(t)/k} as a special case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the cotangent exact sequence to show the dt_i span; linear independence is subtler: construct maps Ω_{K/k}→K sending dt1↦1 and other dti↦0, handled first for simple generations, then finitely generated, then general by direct limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global definition of relative cotangent sheaf Ω_{X/Y}
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism π:X→Y, define Ω_{X/Y} as the conormal sheaf N^∨_{X/X×_Y X} of the diagonal embedding δ:X→X×_Y X. The derivation d:O_X→Ω_{X/Y} is given locally by df = pr2^*f − pr1^*f restricted to the diagonal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This globalizes the affine constructions; one must check compatibility on overlaps. Interpretability: for Y a point and X a manifold, this recovers the usual cotangent bundle via the normal bundle of the diagonal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caution about d: O_X → Ω_{X/Y}
rubrics_metrics.description: The map d is not a morphism of quasicoherent sheaves on X (in the usual sense), though it is O_Y-linear in the only possible meaning. For any open U⊂X, d induces Γ(U,O_X) → Γ(U,Ω_{X/Y}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind this subtlety when treating d globally; the affine checks reconcile the construction with the universal derivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine identification: Ω_{A/B} ≅ I/I^2 for diagonal ideal I
rubrics_metrics.description: For Spec A→Spec B, letting I be the kernel of A⊗_B A → A (diagonal ideal), the natural morphism Ω_{A/B} → I/I^2 induced by the universal property is an isomorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 21.2.22 gives a two-step proof: show surjectivity (da maps to 1⊗a − a⊗1) and construct g:I/I^2 → Ω_{A/B} by x⊗y ↦ x dy and verify well-definedness using Leibniz.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affine-to-global gluing: Γ(Spec A, Ω_{X/Y}) ≅ Ω_{A/B}
rubrics_metrics.description: On an affine open Spec A over Spec B, the global construction restricts to the affine construction: Γ(Spec A, Ω_{X/Y}) ≅ Ω_{A/B}, and the induced d matches the affine derivation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.2.N; this justifies that the global sheaf Ω_{X/Y} glues the affine Ω's.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cotangent exact sequence (Theorem 21.2.23(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: For morphisms X --π--> Y --ρ--> Z, there is an exact sequence of quasicoherent sheaves on X: π^*Ω_{Y/Z} → Ω_{X/Z} → Ω_{X/Y} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This globalizes the affine cotangent exact sequence (Theorem 21.2.9). Expect left-exactness under additional smoothness hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conormal exact sequence (Theorem 21.2.23(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: For a closed embedding i:X↪Y with conormal sheaf N^∨_{X/Y}, and a morphism Y→Z, there is an exact sequence N^∨_{X/Y} → i^*Ω_{Y/Z} → Ω_{X/Z} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This globalizes the affine conormal exact sequence (Theorem 21.2.12). Left-exactness can hold under smoothness hypotheses (see later theorems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exactness under smoothness (Exercise 21.2.S)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cotangent exact sequence is exact on the left if the involved morphisms π and ρ are smooth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The matrix argument used in earlier exercises (block upper triangular) applies; see Exercise 13.6.D for the linear algebra step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback/base-change of Ω (Theorem 21.2.25)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) For a commutative square X' → X over Y' → Y there is a natural map μ^*Ω_{X/Y} → Ω_{X'/Y'}. (b) If the square is Cartesian (X' ≅ X×_Y Y'), then μ^*Ω_{X/Y} ≅ Ω_{X'/Y'}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use affine Exercise 21.2.K to deduce part (b). Important consequence: the fiber of Ω at a point is the Ω of the fiber scheme.

rubrics_metrics.name: Product formula for differentials (Exercise 21.2.U)
rubrics_metrics.description: For fibered product X×_Z Y with projections α',β' etc., there is an isomorphism Ω_{X×_Z Y / Z} ≅ (α')^*Ω_{Y/Z} ⊕ (β')^*Ω_{X/Z} (or similarly written as Ω_{X/Z} ⊕ Ω_{Y/Z}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes how Ω behaves under products; the right-hand direct sum decomposition is often used in computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redefinition of k-smoothness (21.3.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A k-scheme X is smooth of dimension n over k if it is locally of finite type, of pure dimension n, and Ω_{X/k} is locally free of rank n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is compatible with earlier definitions (Exercise 21.3.A). One may omit explicitly stating n and allow disjoint unions of smooth components of various dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smoothness vs regularity over perfect fields (Exercise 21.3.C)
rubrics_metrics.description: If k is perfect and X is a finite type k-scheme, then X is smooth iff X is regular at all closed points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use base change to k̄ and properties of regularity; this yields a concise criterion for smoothness of varieties over perfect fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generic smoothness of varieties (Theorem 21.3.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: If X is an irreducible variety over a perfect field k of dimension n, there exists a dense open U⊂X such that U is smooth of dimension n (i.e., varieties are smooth on a dense open).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof reduces to checking Ω at the generic point: show Ω_{K/k} has dimension n where K is the function field, using separable generation of extensions over perfect fields and Exercise 21.2.M(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobian criterion for algebraic dependence (Exercise 21.3.D)
rubrics_metrics.description: Over a field k of characteristic 0, polynomials f1,...,fn ∈ k[x1,...,xn] are algebraically dependent iff the determinant of the Jacobian matrix is identically zero.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hint: relate to generic smoothness (Theorem 21.3.4). This is a concrete algebraic test for dependence using differentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conormal exact sequence exact on left for smooth embeddings (Theorem 21.3.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: If i:X↪Y is a closed embedding of smooth k-varieties of codimension r, then the conormal exact sequence is exact on the left: 0 → N^∨_{X/Y} → i^*Ω_{Y/k} → Ω_{X/k} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dualizing yields the normal exact sequence 0 → T_X → T_Y|_X → N_{X/Y} → 0. Proof uses that I/I^2 is locally free of rank r (regular embedding) and associated-point arguments exploiting smoothness/regularity at closed points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generality of left-exactness (Remark 21.3.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The conormal sequence is exact on the left in more general contexts than smooth varieties; essentially one needs appropriate smoothness of the embedding i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Stacks Project tags referenced for broader statements; the core requirement is suitable smoothness/hypotheses on i.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of Zariski cotangent space with fiber of Ω at separable point (Corollary 21.3.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a smooth k-variety Y and a closed point q whose residue field κ(q) is separable over k, the conormal exact sequence for q↪Y identifies the Zariski cotangent space at q with the fiber of Ω_{Y/k} at q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This extends Jacobian descriptions of tangent/cotangent spaces to separable closed points; immediate corollary of Theorem 21.3.6 with X=q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of conormal/I/I^2 rank to prove regularity of localizations (21.3.11 & exercises)
rubrics_metrics.description: To show localization of regular local rings are regular (in varieties over perfect fields), analyze I/I^2 at generic/stalk points: its rank equals codimension and identifies with m/m^2 at generic points, yielding regularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine Theorem 21.3.4 (generic smoothness) and Theorem 21.3.6; use Nakayama and classification of modules at discrete valuation rings in related exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geometric genus and canonical bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: For a regular irreducible projective curve C over k, the geometric genus is pg = h^0(C, Ω_{C/k}). More generally, for an n-dimensional smooth variety X, the canonical bundle K_X is det Ω_{X/k} = Ω^n_{X/k} and pg(X)=h^0(X,K_X).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ω is coherent (Exercise 21.2.P) so these H^0 spaces are finite for projective schemes. For curves, pg equals h^1(C,O_C) (Riemann-Roch/Serre duality connections discussed later).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation: Ω_{P^1/k} ≅ O(-2)
rubrics_metrics.description: On P^1_k, the cotangent sheaf Ω_{P^1/k} is isomorphic to O(-2); equivalently the tangent bundle has degree 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute on coordinate patches: dx on one affine patch has a double pole on the other, giving O(-2). This argument works over Z and base-changes; consequence: geometric genus of P^1 is 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentials on hyperelliptic curves and degree of Ω_C/k
rubrics_metrics.description: For a hyperelliptic double cover π:C→P^1 branched at 2g+2 points, the pullback π^*dx has 2g+2 zeros and 4 poles, so deg Ω_{C/k} = 2g-2. One can produce g independent global differentials ω_i and show h^0(C,Ω)=g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises lead to explicit bases ω_i (e.g., x^i dx/y) and valuations computations; this sets up the Riemann-Hurwitz formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentials for discrete valuation rings (DVR) coming from finitely generated k-algebras
rubrics_metrics.description: If (A,m,k) is a DVR that is a localization of a finitely generated k-algebra and t is a uniformizer, then Ω_{A/k} ≅ A·dt (free rank one generated by dt).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 21.4.D outlines steps: show Ω is finitely generated, surject onto dt modulo m using a chosen projection to residue field, apply Nakayama to deduce principal, then use reduction mod t^N to show dt is non-torsion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Euler exact sequence for projective space (Theorem 21.4.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: For P^n_A, there is an exact sequence 0 → Ω_{P^n/A} → O(-1)^{⊕(n+1)} → O → 0. Dualizing gives 0 → O → O(1)^{⊕(n+1)} → T_{P^n/A} → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct the map φ:O(-1)^{n+1}→O(0) by (s0,...,sn)↦Σ x_i s_i; identify kernel with Ω via explicit local formulas on patches (see exercise/proof). This gives a concrete handle on Ω_{P^n}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizations: projective bundles and Grassmannians
rubrics_metrics.description: The Euler sequence generalizes: for a projective bundle P(V) over X with V a rank n+1 vector bundle, Ω_{P(V)/X} sits in an Euler-like exact sequence 0→Ω_{P(V)/X}→O_{P(V)}(-1)⊗π^*V^∨→O_{P(V)}→0. For the Grassmannian G(m,n+1) there is a canonical isomorphism Ω_{G(m,n+1)/k} ≅ Hom(Q,S) where 0→S→O⊗V^∨→Q→0 is the tautological sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These generalizations are useful for computations of normal bundles and in moduli constructions; proofs are analogous to the projective space case and appear in exercises/remarks.
